exposure: Robson 5A category ('unique uterine scar, single cephalic ≥37 weeks')
cohort: 1500 women from Sub-Saharan Africa and 2206 women from France in the PreCARE study (2010-2012)
finding: The difference in cesarean section rates between women from Sub-Saharan Africa and France is largely attributed to the Robson 5A category, and within this group, medical factors alone do not fully explain the increased risk for Sub-Saharan African women.
mod_finding: Within the Robson 5A category, Sub-Saharan African origin was associated with cesarean before labor after adjusting for medical risk factors but not after adjusting for social deprivation; however, it remained associated with cesarean during labor even after adjusting for both medical and social factors.
